item.title: Beast of Reincarnation Release Date & Time
item.description:
Game Freak's first major Action RPG title, Beast of Reincarnation , is almost here, and players around the world are eager to get their hands on the game and try it out for themselves. Available on both console and PC, Beast of Reincarnation officially launches on August 4. However, depending on your region, you may be able to start playing a little earlier. Here's the exact time and date you can expect Beast of Reincarnation to release in your region.

Interview: Beast of Reincarnation Director Discusses the Unexpected Blade Runner Connection

Game Rant sits down with Beast of Reincarnation director Kota Furushima, who touches on, among other things, an unexpected link to a classic film.

By Nick Rodriguez

Beast of Reincarnation releases globally on Tuesday, August 4, 12 AM UTC / Monday, August 3 at 8 PM ET. Since the game has a global release time, you cannot use any kind of regional setting tricks to jump into the game early.

Beast of Reincarnation also does not have an early access period , meaning that players, regardless of whether they have pre-ordered the game or are purchasing at launch, can all expect to jump in at the same time.

item.title: Pokemon TCG Players Can Get Free Pitch Black Cards, But There’s a Catch
item.description:
Pokemon TCG Live is giving away free full-art cards from the game's newest expansion, Pitch Black, though players will need to act fast to claim the cards. The giveaway in the digital trading card game marks the halfway point of the new Pokemon TCG set's cycle.

Fans of the Pokemon Trading Card Game have no shortage of options to collect cards and battle with others beyond the physical game. Pokemon TCG Pocket saw massive success after its launch in late 2024 as a simplified version of the game, featuring brand-new cards and daily free packs for fans playing the game. Pokemon TCG Live mirrors the physical TCG with its gameplay and card selection, created as an online simulator using the same cards and expansions. Now, fans on TCG Live can pick up free cards and a free pack in the game for a limited time.

Pokemon TCG Shop Offers Cash Bounty for Thief's Capture

A burgled Pokemon TCG store takes matters into its own hands by offering a cash bounty reward to anyone who successfully catches the thief.

By Sarah Fields

Pokemon TCG Live is Giving Away Free Full-Art Cards

  • ENDLESSNIGHT26
  • Ultra Rare Mega Zeraora ex, Ultra Rare Mega Excadrill ex, 1 pack of Pitch Black
  • Available until September 16, 10:00 a.m. PDT

Pokemon TCG Live has rolled out its official mid-expansion passcode for the Pitch Black set, giving away cards and a free pack. Players can use the code "ENDLESSNIGHT26" to redeem the Ultra Rare full-art versions of both Mega Zeraora ex and Mega Excadrill ex in the digital game. The code also comes with one free pack of Pitch Black that players can open after redeeming, potentially containing cards like the Mega Hyper Rare and Special Illustration Rare versions of Mega Darkrai ex. Fans of Pokemon TCG Live can claim their free cards by using the redemption code in the in-game shop, though the code is set to expire on September 16 at 10:00 a.m. PDT.

The newest redemption code gives players a pair of powerful cards to put in their Pokemon TCG Live decks. Mega Zeraora ex can be a devastating damage dealer when allowed to set up, with its Thunderous Fist attack doing an additional 60 damage for each Lightning Energy attached to Zeraora. Mega Excadrill can put out similarly strong damage with its Maximum Drilling attack, dealing 330 damage when two extra Energy cards are attached to the Pokemon, in addition to the three Metal Energy required. Steel-type decks also feature a variety of powerful tools for ramping Energies, including Metang and Steven's Metagross ex pulling Energies from the deck.

The one pack of Pitch Black included with the code can also give players access to a variety of new cards. Pitch Black introduced five new Supporter cards to the Pokemon TCG , including both new characters from Pokemon Legends: Z-A , such as Gwynn and Jett, and older Trainers like Misty and Gladion. The expansion has six different Special Illustration Rare cards that players can pull, including new Mega Pokemon like Mega Chandelure and Mega Zeraora and a new card of fan-favorite Pokemon Morpeko.

Pitch Black serves as the precursor to arguably the most highly-anticipated Pokemon set of the year. The Pokemon TCG will officially debut the 30th Celebration expansion in early September, serving as the game's tribute to the 30th anniversary of the franchise. 30th Celebration not only features reprints of some of the most iconic cards from throughout the Pokemon TCG 's history, but also debuts a brand-new rarity with the colorful Futuristic Rare versions of Mewtwo and Mew. Pokemon TCG fans should have plenty to look forward to throughout the rest of 2026, with some big releases on the way for the game.

item.title: 5 Forgotten 2000s RPGs That Are Perfect From Start To Finish
item.description:
The 2000s was a critical time for the gaming industry. The monstrously successful PlayStation 2 arrived in 2000, with Microsoft's first Xbox system and Nintendo's iconic GameCube launching in North America the following year. This set the stage for a console generation marked by a fascinating three-way competition, and of course, some brilliant games. In particular, RPG fans had an embarrassment of riches to enjoy during the 2000s.

How Modern Easter Eggs in Video Games Have Changed From the Late 90s, Early 2000s

From playground rumors to Reddit threads, the changing nature of Easter Eggs has shaped how gamers interact with their favorite video games.

By Carla Carmona

Then as now, though, it's just impossible to play all the games we'd like to. Even if you've been an RPG enthusiast for decades, there are some great games from this era that may have passed you by. These five titles, for instance, are still more than worth a playthrough today. With unique gameplay mechanics, engaging stories and varied takes on combat, they're required reading (or rather, playing) for genre fans.

The PlayStation family of systems were especially rich with great RPGs during this time, so there's quite a heavy focus on Sony systems on this list. Note, too, that these "perfect" titles aren't strictly free of cons and downsides, but rather superb titles that were about as good as they could reasonably be at the time.

5 Vagrant Story

Explore The Dark and Fascinating City of Leá Monde

Follow
Followed
Vagrant Story
JRPG

May 15, 2000

WHERE TO PLAY

Square Enix seems to love experimenting with the role-playing concept, both mechanically and visually. This has led to intriguing recent releases like Dungeon Encounters in 2021 and the Voice of Cards trilogy. Long before these games, when the company was still simply known as Square, it released Vagrant Story in 2000. Riskbreaker Ashley Riot's quest to pursue a cult leader in the afflicted city of Leá Monde is one of the most complex and fascinating RPGs in the company's wide library.

What fascinates me the most about Vagrant Story is the way it combines elements from so many different genres. With its dark, supernatural vibe and sprawling tombs to explore, it always felt to me more of a dungeon crawler. To reach the next area, or a distant door at the end of a chamber, you'll often need to do a little platforming. Ashley is quite stiff to control, which can make segments like these a bit awkward, but this owes more to the sheer ambition of the title.

If there's one thing I can never resist in an RPG, it's a deep, customizable battle system, and this is where Vagrant Story excels. Ashley can freely move around the environment, but attacking brings up a menu in which the player has to choose specific body parts of foes to target. This is how you hit weaknesses, prevent the use of specific abilities, negate movement, and so on. Weapon varieties, from swords to polearms, each have their own strengths and weaknesses, so it's important to have a varied arsenal that you can switch up as needed. This is where the workshop comes in, a deep and engrossing mechanic in its own right. I spent a lot of time in my own playthrough tweaking each weapon and adjusting its characteristics, and the constantly changing enemies

4 Wizardry 8

An Epic Quest in a Fantastical World

Followed
Wizardry 8
Adventure
RPG
Systems
Released
November 15, 2001
ESRB
T // Blood and Gore, Violence
Developer(s)
Sir-tech Software, Inc.
Publisher(s)
NightDive Studios, Drecom Co., Ltd.

WHERE TO PLAY

DIGITAL

Genre(s)
Adventure, RPG
Platform(s)
Windows, macOS
Powered by

There are some classic titles that, upon a revisit, really show you how much they influenced the games that came after them. For me, Wizardry 8 is a great example. While the CRPG faithful may fondly remember this one, the broader world of gaming probably won't. It's a shame, because this 2001 release from Sir-Tech Canada was a marvel.

As the title makes clear, there were many Wizardry sequels before it, but this was the eighth and final mainline installment from the western team (though not the end of the series itself). It begins in grand fashion, with an enigmatic narrator announcing, "before the beginning, the Cosmic Lords crafted three artifacts," detailing how this trio of items was the key to the creation of worlds. Though hidden away by the Lords across galaxies, they were separately stolen. The player's objective, then, is to journey between worlds and assemble them all. At which point they can, as promised in the intro, "become Cosmic Lords themselves."

The 10 Most Powerful Wizards In Fiction, Ranked

Merlin, Gandalf, Dumbledore, and Vivi are just a few of the most overpowered wizards in the history of fiction, from legends to movies and games.

By Alfredo Robelo

The party explores from a first-person perspective, through classic locales such as monasteries, temples, taverns, and an eerie graveyard. Battles against foes are a little fiddly to organize, with party members having their own menus and inventories, but there's a satisfying weight to the whole adventure that's part dungeon crawler and part point and click. The skill development, which sees party members advance in various skills like Sword, Close Combat, Mythology, and Communication, will be extremely familiar to fans of the likes of Skyrim , and though it certainly feels its age today, this is a classic quest that tells a gripping, magical tale.

3 Skies of Arcadia Legends

The Definitive Skies of Arcadia Experience

Skies of Arcadia: Legends
Released
January 29, 2003

Platform(s)
GameCube
Powered by

During this era, as noted, the JRPG genre found something of a natural home on PlayStation systems. The GameCube and Xbox still saw some excellent entries of their own, though, and Skies of Arcadia Legends was a bit of a coup for Nintendo's system. An upgraded port, it brought a new character and extended story, additional mechanics, and used the benefit of hindsight to address some bugbears with the original Skies of Arcadia (most prominently the rate of those pesky random battles).

This is the story of Vyse and the Blue Rogues, a well-meaning band of air pirates who are thrust into conflict with the mighty Valuan Empire. The empire believes it can bring the whole realm under its control by harnessing the power of the Moon Crystals, and so the pirates mobilize to defeat its forces and prevent it from capturing these artifacts. For me, the twists and turns, the narrow escapes and last-minute rescues, all leading to a climactic battle and ultimate success, are all the best JRPG tropes firing in style. This extends to the battles, which revolve around adjusting to the attributes of enemies and ensuring that you have a varied range of your own so you can always hit a weakness.

There's a bright, colorful vibe about Legends from the very beginning, a whimsical quality that some genre entries can really lack. It doesn't take itself too seriously, but nor is it afraid to hit some heart-wrenching story beats. Some prominent characters die in ways I didn't foresee at all, and it was quite shocking. All in all, this is a JRPG with super solid mechanics and an awful lot of heart and charm, and because it's a 2002 GameCube-only port of a Dreamcast title from 2000, many genre fans never got a chance to experience it.

2 Shadow Hearts: Covenant

A Supernatural World War One Thriller

Shadow Hearts: Covenant
JRPG
Systems
Released
September 27, 2004
ESRB
T For Teen Due To Language, Partial Nudity, Suggestive Themes, Violence
Developer(s)
Nautilus
Publisher(s)
Aruze, Midway Games
Franchise
Shadow Hearts

WHERE TO PLAY

PHYSICAL

Genre(s)
JRPG
Platform(s)
PlayStation 2
Powered by

Nautilus' 2004 RPG Shadow Hearts: Covenant follows on from the first title. It presents a take on the horrors of World War One, set in a world of time travel and demonic forces. These are concepts that I've only really seen combined elsewhere in Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem , during Peter Jacobs' chapter of the game, and it had me intrigued from the beginning. There's much more to the Shadow Hearts games than just a novel setting, though.

With some RPGs, I find that the story pacing really doesn't match my tastes, and there are certain sections that I'll choose to rush through without paying much attention on a replay. Covenant , however, kept me gripped throughout. Rasputin's plans with the otherworldly force of Asmodeus and cosmic forces' efforts to manipulate the course of the human war give the conflict a grander scale, but the stakes are so very human too. This is evidenced by its ending, which potentially allows one of our heroes a second chance to save their partner Alice Elliot, a victim of the Four Masks' Curse (if the player received the bad ending) in Shadow Hearts .

8 Long PS2 Games That Take Forever To Complete, Officially Ranked

Explore the longest PS2 games, from JRPGs to racing games, offering massive amounts of content to keep you playing for days, weeks, or even months.

By Evan Regan

In the party's quest to end the machinations of Rasputin and his allies, the party will face many turn-based battles. These, for me, are some of the most unique of the era. In another similarity to Eternal Darkness , a Sanity Meter is at play, this time during combat. If it's not carefully managed alongside the usual hit points and magic reserves, party members can become uncontrollable. If this happens during a crucial encounter, it could spell your doom. An additional mechanic called the Judgment Ring asks the player to carefully 'aim' their sklills and attacks as they activate them, for added potency. As such, it's vital to carefully manage the ebb and flow of combat from the first battle to the last. A lot of PS2 titles are genuine 10/10s, and I might just add this one to the list too.

1 Jeanne d'Arc

An Underappreciated TRPG Classic

Follow
Followed
Jeanne d'Arc
Tactical
Systems
Released
November 22, 2006
ESRB
T Due To Alcohol Reference, Fantasy Violence, Mild Language
Developer(s)
Level 5
Publisher(s)
Sony Computer Entertainment

WHERE TO PLAY

DIGITAL
PHYSICAL

Genre(s)
Tactical
Platform(s)
PlayStation Portable, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5
Powered by

Another title for a PlayStation system, this time the PSP. Much like PS Vita after it, this handheld would see a wealth of excellent RPGs and strategy games, and Jeanne d'Arc is one that just doesn't get the attention it deserves. A turn-based strategy game from Level-5 (of Professor Layton fame), it's super loosely based on the Hundred Years War between the French and the English, and the titular character's enormous importance in the former's cause.

As Jeanne and her French allies, the player will campaign across the map gathering their forces and bringing the fight to the English, who have allied themselves with the same demonic forces that humanity once banded together to banish. The game has a look and feel that's very Final Fantasy Tactics -esque, but it also implemented some unique mechanics to ensure that it isn't just a retread of the genre mechanics that came before.

Right from the start, I delighted in the way that the burning aura mechanic encouraged me to focus the attacks of my unit. I struggle with balancing the right turn order in these kinds of games, and this idea works brilliantly to make subsequent attacks and skills more powerful against targets. Defending in groups is also rewarded, in a manner similar to the spirit wall mechanic used in Skulls of the Shogun . Though the polished turn-based action is the primary focus of Jeanne d'Arc , there's a huge emotional weight to its campaign as well, with the devastation of the surrounding regions and the impact of the conflict away from the battlefield itself showcased too. Just one more lesser-known classic for the PSP.

5 Open-World RPGs That Are Perfect Masterpieces

From immersive historical epics to Soulsborne masterpieces and isometric gems, these open-world RPGs are as good as the genre gets.

By Mark Sammut

If there's one thing I can never resist in an RPG, it's a deep, customizable battle system, and this is where Vagrant Story excels. Ashley can freely move around the environment, but attacking brings up a menu in which the player has to choose specific body parts of foes to target. This is how you hit weaknesses, prevent the use of specific abilities, negate movement, and so on. Weapon varieties, from swords to polearms, each have their own strengths and weaknesses, so it's important to have a varied arsenal that you can switch up as needed. This is where the workshop comes in, a deep and engrossing mechanic in its own right. I spent a lot of time in my own playthrough tweaking each weapon and adjusting its characteristics, and the constantly changing enemies

4 Wizardry 8

An Epic Quest in a Fantastical World

Follow
Followed
Wizardry 8
Adventure
RPG
Systems
Released
November 15, 2001
ESRB
T // Blood and Gore, Violence
Developer(s)
Sir-tech Software, Inc.
Publisher(s)
NightDive Studios, Drecom Co., Ltd.

WHERE TO PLAY

DIGITAL

Genre(s)
Adventure, RPG
Platform(s)
Windows, macOS
Powered by

There are some classic titles that, upon a revisit, really show you how much they influenced the games that came after them. For me, Wizardry 8 is a great example. While the CRPG faithful may fondly remember this one, the broader world of gaming probably won't. It's a shame, because this 2001 release from Sir-Tech Canada was a marvel.

As the title makes clear, there were many Wizardry sequels before it, but this was the eighth and final mainline installment from the western team (though not the end of the series itself). It begins in grand fashion, with an enigmatic narrator announcing, "before the beginning, the Cosmic Lords crafted three artifacts," detailing how this trio of items was the key to the creation of worlds. Though hidden away by the Lords across galaxies, they were separately stolen. The player's objective, then, is to journey between worlds and assemble them all. At which point they can, as promised in the intro, "become Cosmic Lords themselves."

The 10 Most Powerful Wizards In Fiction, Ranked

Merlin, Gandalf, Dumbledore, and Vivi are just a few of the most overpowered wizards in the history of fiction, from legends to movies and games.

By Alfredo Robelo

The party explores from a first-person perspective, through classic locales such as monasteries, temples, taverns, and an eerie graveyard. Battles against foes are a little fiddly to organize, with party members having their own menus and inventories, but there's a satisfying weight to the whole adventure that's part dungeon crawler and part point and click. The skill development, which sees party members advance in various skills like Sword, Close Combat, Mythology, and Communication, will be extremely familiar to fans of the likes of Skyrim , and though it certainly feels its age today, this is a classic quest that tells a gripping, magical tale.

3 Skies of Arcadia Legends

The Definitive Skies of Arcadia Experience

Skies of Arcadia: Legends
Released
January 29, 2003

Platform(s)
GameCube
Powered by

During this era, as noted, the JRPG genre found something of a natural home on PlayStation systems. The GameCube and Xbox still saw some excellent entries of their own, though, and Skies of Arcadia Legends was a bit of a coup for Nintendo's system. An upgraded port, it brought a new character and extended story, additional mechanics, and used the benefit of hindsight to address some bugbears with the original Skies of Arcadia (most prominently the rate of those pesky random battles).

This is the story of Vyse and the Blue Rogues, a well-meaning band of air pirates who are thrust into conflict with the mighty Valuan Empire. The empire believes it can bring the whole realm under its control by harnessing the power of the Moon Crystals, and so the pirates mobilize to defeat its forces and prevent it from capturing these artifacts. For me, the twists and turns, the narrow escapes and last-minute rescues, all leading to a climactic battle and ultimate success, are all the best JRPG tropes firing in style. This extends to the battles, which revolve around adjusting to the attributes of enemies and ensuring that you have a varied range of your own so you can always hit a weakness.

There's a bright, colorful vibe about Legends from the very beginning, a whimsical quality that some genre entries can really lack. It doesn't take itself too seriously, but nor is it afraid to hit some heart-wrenching story beats. Some prominent characters die in ways I didn't foresee at all, and it was quite shocking. All in all, this is a JRPG with super solid mechanics and an awful lot of heart and charm, and because it's a 2002 GameCube-only port of a Dreamcast title from 2000, many genre fans never got a chance to experience it.

2 Shadow Hearts: Covenant

A Supernatural World War One Thriller

Shadow Hearts: Covenant
JRPG
Systems
Released
September 27, 2004
ESRB
T For Teen Due To Language, Partial Nudity, Suggestive Themes, Violence
Developer(s)
Nautilus
Publisher(s)
Aruze, Midway Games
Franchise
Shadow Hearts

WHERE TO PLAY

PHYSICAL

Genre(s)
JRPG
Platform(s)
PlayStation 2
Powered by

Nautilus' 2004 RPG Shadow Hearts: Covenant follows on from the first title. It presents a take on the horrors of World War One, set in a world of time travel and demonic forces. These are concepts that I've only really seen combined elsewhere in Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem , during Peter Jacobs' chapter of the game, and it had me intrigued from the beginning. There's much more to the Shadow Hearts games than just a novel setting, though.

With some RPGs, I find that the story pacing really doesn't match my tastes, and there are certain sections that I'll choose to rush through without paying much attention on a replay. Covenant , however, kept me gripped throughout. Rasputin's plans with the otherworldly force of Asmodeus and cosmic forces' efforts to manipulate the course of the human war give the conflict a grander scale, but the stakes are so very human too. This is evidenced by its ending, which potentially allows one of our heroes a second chance to save their partner Alice Elliot, a victim of the Four Masks' Curse (if the player received the bad ending) in Shadow Hearts .

8 Long PS2 Games That Take Forever To Complete, Officially Ranked

Explore the longest PS2 games, from JRPGs to racing games, offering massive amounts of content to keep you playing for days, weeks, or even months.

By Evan Regan

In the party's quest to end the machinations of Rasputin and his allies, the party will face many turn-based battles. These, for me, are some of the most unique of the era. In another similarity to Eternal Darkness , a Sanity Meter is at play, this time during combat. If it's not carefully managed alongside the usual hit points and magic reserves, party members can become uncontrollable. If this happens during a crucial encounter, it could spell your doom. An additional mechanic called the Judgment Ring asks the player to carefully 'aim' their sklills and attacks as they activate them, for added potency. As such, it's vital to carefully manage the ebb and flow of combat from the first battle to the last. A lot of PS2 titles are genuine 10/10s, and I might just add this one to the list too.

1 Jeanne d'Arc

An Underappreciated TRPG Classic

Follow
Followed
Jeanne d'Arc
Tactical
Systems
Released
November 22, 2006
ESRB
T Due To Alcohol Reference, Fantasy Violence, Mild Language
Developer(s)
Level 5
Publisher(s)
Sony Computer Entertainment

WHERE TO PLAY

DIGITAL
PHYSICAL

Genre(s)
Tactical
Platform(s)
PlayStation Portable, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5
Powered by

Another title for a PlayStation system, this time the PSP. Much like PS Vita after it, this handheld would see a wealth of excellent RPGs and strategy games, and Jeanne d'Arc is one that just doesn't get the attention it deserves. A turn-based strategy game from Level-5 (of Professor Layton fame), it's super loosely based on the Hundred Years War between the French and the English, and the titular character's enormous importance in the former's cause.

As Jeanne and her French allies, the player will campaign across the map gathering their forces and bringing the fight to the English, who have allied themselves with the same demonic forces that humanity once banded together to banish. The game has a look and feel that's very Final Fantasy Tactics -esque, but it also implemented some unique mechanics to ensure that it isn't just a retread of the genre mechanics that came before.

Right from the start, I delighted in the way that the burning aura mechanic encouraged me to focus the attacks of my unit. I struggle with balancing the right turn order in these kinds of games, and this idea works brilliantly to make subsequent attacks and skills more powerful against targets. Defending in groups is also rewarded, in a manner similar to the spirit wall mechanic used in Skulls of the Shogun . Though the polished turn-based action is the primary focus of Jeanne d'Arc , there's a huge emotional weight to its campaign as well, with the devastation of the surrounding regions and the impact of the conflict away from the battlefield itself showcased too. Just one more lesser-known classic for the PSP.

5 Open-World RPGs That Are Perfect Masterpieces

From immersive historical epics to Soulsborne masterpieces and isometric gems, these open-world RPGs are as good as the genre gets.

By Mark Sammut

item.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 PlayStation Accounts Being Compromised By Hacker
item.description:
The Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 multiplayer servers on PS5 and PS4 have been compromised by a hacker that has gone around several lobbies and manipulated player accounts. The reports came weeks after Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 and its predecessor were shadow-dropped on the PlayStation Store across the globe.

Although it was released on the PS3 in 2013, Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 was unavailable for most PlayStation players for several years due to the PS4 and PS5 not including backward compatibility with the PS3. Ergo, players who wanted to experience the first two entries in the Call of Duty: Black Ops series had to use other platforms, such as Steam and Xbox. On July 9, Black Ops 1 and 2 were released as direct ports by Iron Galaxy Studios, who worked alongside Activision and Treyarch. Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 support cross-generation matchmaking across the PS5 and PS4 ecosystems, though this does not extend to full cross play with other systems.

Call of Duty Fans Just Discovered Cut Black Ops Zombies Content

Call of Duty: Black Ops players discover cut Zombies content more than 15 years later, offering a rare look at Treyarch’s early experiments.

By Adrian Morales

Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 Servers Become a Hacker's Playground

However, cheaters still run rampant within the PlayStation ports of Black Ops 1 and 2 . As reported by GamesRadar+, Call of Duty: Black Ops 2' s multiplayer lobbies still rely on vulnerable infrastructure that has not been upgraded since the game's initial 2013 launch. A hacker who goes by the aliases "C Isn't Sharp" and "Who Isn't Sharp?" has reportedly appeared in player lobbies to mess with player accounts in different ways. While some users have had their levels and Prestige ranks altered by C Isn't Sharp, others stated that they have been unable to go back into matches due to game crashes that occurred afterward.

Even high-profile content creators have not been spared by C Isn't Sharp. Twitch and YouTube streamer TimTheTatman shared a clip from a recent broadcast that saw his account boosted to level 55 and Prestige 16, with the latter rank being one that does not exist at all in Black Ops 2 . TimTheTatman took to social media afterward and tagged the Call of Duty development team to raise awareness on the issue. In response to TimTheTatman's post, several Call of Duty players condemned the hacker's actions.

Despite the ongoing issues with Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 's multiplayer lobbies, that has not stopped the PlayStation ports from selling well. Although Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 are priced at $40 each on the PlayStation Store, Black Ops 2 had over five million PSN players logging in from across the US. During the initial launch, the PS5 port of Black Ops 2 even outpaced other Call of Duty titles, such as Black Ops 7 and Warzone , on Sony's current-gen platform.

As of this writing, neither Activision, Treyarch, nor Iron Galaxy have publicly commented on the ongoing situation with the PlayStation ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 . Though the developers have largely pivoted toward the upcoming open beta of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , it remains to be seen what steps the developers will take to address the problem.

item.title: Steam Update Officially Adds New Steam Deck Feature
item.description:
A new update to the Steam Deck is adding a popular feature to Valve's handheld console, with the system set to support HDR graphics for the first time. The update comes as a Steam Beta patch exclusive to the OLED model of the Steam Deck, with wider implementation likely coming later.

The Steam Deck was one of the hottest new consoles on the market when the handheld gaming system officially released in 2022. The handheld console supports a wide variety of games from the online marketplace's library, with more games regularly being verified to run on the platform. Rumors have even suggested that Valve may be planning a successor to the Steam Deck, though it has confirmed that any new edition would have to be a major upgrade from the original. Now, the Steam Deck is set to receive a nice new update that should make games look even better on the console.

Epic Games CEO Throws Shade at Valve Over the Steam Deck Price Hike

Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney has harsh words for Valve regarding the company's recently announced price increase for the Steam Deck.

By Michael Brandon Ingram

Valve is Adding HDR Support to the Steam Deck

A new Steam Beta update has officially added HDR support to the Steam Deck's OLED model. The patch will allow the handheld console to apply HDR settings to games when using Remote Play on Steam to stream games to the handheld console from a connected PC. The update also adds experimental support for streaming AV1 video, said to be able to deliver higher image quality when streaming while taking up less bandwidth. The update also came with several smaller fixes for a variety of features on the Steam Deck, ranging from Remote Play and Local Network Game Transfers to improving video color range.

The new improvements to Steam Deck should benefit a wide variety of games that can make use of HDR. HDR offers major upgrades to a variety of graphical systems, ranging from improving the range of colors in games to greater depth to a game's lighting elements. HDR can be a particularly major boon to many games going for ultra-realistic artstyles, including popular titles like Death Stranding 2: On the Beach and Marvel's Spider-Man 2 . At release, the Steam Deck's new HDR capabilities will likely be limited to Remote Play, with no confirmation about whether standalone support will be added later.

The Steam Deck's graphical capabilities are set to take a big step forward, though the console is now getting pricier for new fans. Valve officially rolled out a major price change for the Steam Deck in late May 2026, increasing the cost for fans to pick up several models of the console. The 512 GB OLED model of the console saw a huge spike with the adjustment, increasing from $549 up to $789 for the cheapest model of the console. The price of the 1TB model rose by similarly staggering totals, rising by $300 to a price tag of $949.

Steam Update Officially Adds New Steam Deck Feature
Steam Users Can Claim Roguelike Game with Very Positive Reviews Before It's Gone

While the Steam Deck saw significant price hikes, Valve also recently debuted its newest Steam-supported console. The long-awaited launch of the Steam Machine finally arrived on June 29, supporting every Steam Deck-verified game and seeing Valve simplify the process of verifying games for the console. Valve's newest console does feature a steep price point of its own, however, with the Steam Machine starting at $1,049 for the 512 GB model of the console. Valve's foray into the console market has largely been a successful venture, albeit a pricey one for fans of Steam.
